title: Emrys and the Harbor
premise: Orsen Crane, a woman living as a man to survive, carries the last diplomatic dispatches of the collapsing Republic of Vessany aboard a river packet bound for neutral Harborton. When census taker Emrys Vale notices discrepancies in her papers and asks one question too many, Orsen must decide whether to silence him or trust him with everything. As victors' historians arrive to write the official record, Orsen races to deposit the true account—of the republic's fall and her own hidden life—with the harbor's archive before the river ice breaks and the victors seal the crossings. She succeeds at terrible cost: her identity enters the record under her own name, but she surrenders the anonymity that kept her alive.
about_author: Oscar Eastwick is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing diplomatic correspondence from collapsed states. He writes historical fiction about the people history almost forgot to record.

chapters.title: The Last Packet
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Orsen Crane, boarding the river packet Meridian with sealed dispatches sewn into her coat lining. She keeps busy hands—mending, whittling—to avoid conversation. Emotional beat: controlled dread beneath practiced calm as the republic's last colors come down behind her.

chapters.title: A Man of Few Answers
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV continues as she navigates the packet's close quarters, deflecting questions about her past with rehearsed biography. A fellow passenger's casual kindness nearly undoes her. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened by the realization that no one alive knows who she truly is.

chapters.title: The Census Taker
chapters.summary: Emrys Vale, a meticulous harbor-district census taker, boards mid-river to update manifests. His POV: he notices 'Orsen Crane' appears in no prior registry he can recall. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into something more personal when their eyes meet over his ledger.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Emrys asks where Crane was registered before the war; Orsen gives an answer that checks out too perfectly. His POV lingers on the flawlessness itself. Emotional beat: the first crack—Emrys suspects, and Orsen sees that he suspects.

chapters.title: Ice on the Rigging
chapters.summary: A storm strands the packet at a frozen waystation. Shared watch duty forces Orsen and Emrys into long conversation; she tells him half-truths about the fall of Vessany. Emotional beat: unexpected warmth, and terror at feeling it.

chapters.title: What the Dispatches Say
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV: alone, she reads fragments of the dispatches she carries—orders that prove the republic's ministers sold the peace terms. Emotional beat: disillusionment; she risks her life for documents that indict the men who sent her.

chapters.title: The Harbor at Last
chapters.summary: Arrival in Harborton, a neutral port city swollen with refugees and victors' officials. Emrys's POV as he files his census sheets and cannot stop thinking about Crane. Emotional beat: separation anxiety disguised as bureaucratic unease.

chapters.title: Papers, Please
chapters.summary: Orsen seeks lodging and contacts for her delivery; checkpoint officers scrutinize men of military age. Her forged exemption papers pass—but barely. Emotional beat: claustrophobic fear that her disguise will fail in a city this full of eyes.

chapters.title: The Historians Arrive
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV: victors' historians requisition harbor records, including his census ledgers, to build their official narrative. He realizes his notes on Crane could expose or protect her. Emotional beat: dawning weight of small paper's power over lives.

chapters.title: An Old Contact
chapters.summary: Orsen meets her handler's cutout, a tavern-keeper named Bess, only to learn the archive courier network has been rolled up. Emotional beat: abandonment—the chain she trusted is broken, and she is now evidence walking.

chapters.title: Ledger Crossings
chapters.summary: Emrys, auditing his own records against the historians' demands, finds Crane's registration gap widening into an official flag. His POV wrestles with duty to the new state versus conscience. Emotional beat: complicity knocking at his door.

chapters.title: The Question Again
chapters.summary: Emrys confronts Orsen privately—not to report her but to understand. She tells him she was born Orsena, that survival required becoming someone else. Emotional beat: raw vulnerability; the mask comes off for one person, once.

chapters.title: Bargains in Smoke
chapters.summary: Bess offers a smuggler's route out—for the dispatches as payment. Orsen refuses to hand truth to profiteers. Emotional beat: hardening resolve; she chooses principle over escape.

chapters.title: The Historian's Offer
chapters.summary: Historian Aldous Renwick summons Emrys, offering protection in exchange for everything he knows about 'the courier.' Emrys stalls. Emotional beat: moral vertigo—he is now the hinge of her fate.

chapters.title: What Survives
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV: hiding in the harbor archives after hours, she drafts her true testimony—the republic's betrayal and her own name—in cipher and plain script. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose; writing as resurrection.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Tavern
chapters.summary: Bess, pressed by victors' agents, reveals Orsen's location. Orsen escapes through the fish-market rooftops but loses the satchel copy of her testimony. Emotional beat: panic and fury; the net closing.

chapters.title: The Ice Begins to Break
chapters.summary: Spring thaw cracks the river; the victors will seal crossings within days. Emrys burns his flagged ledger page and instead enters a corrected record naming Orsena Crane as witness. Emotional beat: quiet defiance—paper as sanctuary.

chapters.title: Renwick's Net
chapters.summary: Renwick corners Emrys with evidence of his falsification, offering clemency if he produces the courier. Emrys's POV: he agrees—and plans to lead them astray. Emotional beat: fear braided with courage.

chapters.title: The Archive Door
chapters.summary: Climax begins: Orsen makes for the harbor archive's deposition office as agents sweep the district. Emrys misdirects the search party down the coal quay. Emotional beat: breathless convergence of every thread.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Climax: Orsen, cornered in the deposition hall, swears her testimony aloud before the assistant registrar just as Renwick arrives—too late; the record is sealed and timestamped. Emotional beat: triumphant stillness amid chaos.

chapters.title: The Price
chapters.summary: Falling action: Orsen is detained but not disappeared—the public record shields her. Emrys accepts suspension and investigation. They part at the ice-choked quay, neither promising what they cannot give. Emotional beat: bittersweet cost of truth.

chapters.title: Emrys and the Harbor
chapters.summary: Epilogue, years later: Emrys, restored to a modest post, finds Orsena Crane's deposition cited in a revisionist history—and a letter from her, alive under her own name in a free town. Emotional beat: belonging achieved not through safety, but through being known.
